real_conflicts: The unity_consistency proposal to 'remove the scattered white dots and thin curved lines' directly undermines the mandate for expressive variation. These elements are the primary source of texture and 'fragmented perception' in the artwork; removing them flattens the visual language into a single, static gradient orb, making the design even more generic and less distinctive.

The simplicity_legibility focus on increasing font sizes and contrast for the footer, while necessary for clarity, risks further homogenizing the page. If all text elements are pushed toward the same high-contrast, high-legibility standard, the subtle atmospheric hierarchy that gives the page its 'immersive' quality will be lost, resulting in a flat, corporate look.
accepted: The completeness_density proposal to move 'Opening Hours' and 'Location' into the main left-hand column is accepted. This allows for a more expressive use of the bottom footer space (which can be used for a larger, more atmospheric graphic element or a more distinct typographic treatment) while keeping essential information in the primary reading path.

The unity_consistency suggestion to replace the generic large gradient orb with a more structured abstract form (like fragmented rings) is accepted, provided it is executed with the 'sharper, high-contrast' elements I proposed to maintain focal distinctiveness.
concession: I concede that the current artwork, while atmospheric, is too passive. It needs to be more active and structurally distinct to truly represent 'fragmented perception' rather than just 'soft light'. I will support the move toward a more structured form, as long as it retains the necessary visual tension and contrast.
compromise: Instead of simply removing the dots and lines (unity) or just making them bigger (simplicity), we will integrate them into the new 'structured' form. The 'fragmented rings' proposed by unity will be the core, but the 'scattered dots' will be re-contextualized as 'debris' or 'fragments' breaking away from these rings. This creates a dynamic, high-contrast focal point (my mandate) that is structurally cohesive (unity) and visually distinct from the clean typography (simplicity).
nonnegotiable: The artwork must break its rectangular containment. It must bleed into the text column or the background to create the 'spatial tension' and 'fragmentation' required by the brief. A contained box is a failure of the 'immersive' mandate.
